**Triage: lands in `packages/platform-objects` ⇒ `domain:metadata`.** Type **Bug** — every user in every locale reads a stale widget title; the declared string reaches nobody. `pm:queue`.

Both halves land in the same package, which is what makes this one card rather than two: the four bundles are `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/*.ts`, and the parity assertion's natural home is that package's own `app-nav-translation-parity.test.ts` — the gate this card shows to be key-set-only.

**Scope fence — dispatchable half only.** Two things in the body are *not* the same size, and only the first is queued here:

1. ✅ **In scope.** Correct the four stale `widget_recent_events` titles to the declared source string, give the two same-titled tiles (`widget_events_by_type` pie, `widget_recent_events` table) distinguishable names — shipping one label twice is the bug the stale translation was accidentally masking — and add the **default-locale content-parity assertion**: `en.ts` must match the declared source string exactly. That last one is cheap and non-controversial precisely because `en` is a copy rather than a translation, which is the invariant the generated half already enforces by rewriting `en` every run. It would have caught this instance.

2. ⛔ **Not in scope.** Stale-marking for *translated* locales when a source string changes. The card is right that this is a real design question — it needs a decision on what a stale translation should do (serve the stale value, fall back to source, fail the build), and that is a maintainer call, not a dev's. **Do not design it inside this card.** If the work convinces you it is needed, file it separately and link back; do not widen this PR into it.

⚠️ **Explicitly forbidden:** regenerating these four bundles. `scripts/i18n-extract.config.ts` documents why the `apps`/`dashboards`/`pages` half is hand-authored — a regenerate deletes ~40 live nav translations per locale. Leaf-value edits only.

Related and **not** to be fixed here: #8543 (the generated-side merge-mode hole this mirrors).

**ACCEPT** — PR #8767. All three in-scope items landed, the fence held, and the positive control is stronger than the one I asked for.

## The positive control went beyond the brief, in the right direction

I asked for one thing: show the `en`-parity assertion actually fails when source and `en.ts` disagree. It was broken **three** ways, and the second is the one I did not think to ask for:

| mutation | result |
|:--|:--|
| `en.ts` value dragged back to the stale title | RED on that path |
| **the SOURCE moved instead** | RED on that path — *"the claim is symmetric, not one-sided"* |
| an `en.ts` app nav label suffixed `(stale)` | RED on that path |

A one-sided assertion would have caught translation drift and missed source drift — the direction this very card's defect arrived from is *source moved, bundle didn't*, so a check that only watched the bundle would have been half a gate wearing a whole gate's name.

**And the measurement reproduces the card's thesis exactly:** each run reported **1 failed, 23 passed** — the 23 pre-existing key-set claims stayed green under every stale value. That is the blindness this card was filed about, demonstrated rather than asserted, and then closed.

## The tile rename is better reasoned than my suggestion

I suggested letting the pie keep the broad name. The dev did that but for a sharper reason than mine: the pair now splits on **what each one adds** — the pie keeps `Audit Events by Action` (the share picture), the table becomes `Event Volume by Action`, which is what its `values: ['event_count']` actually produces and what its own description already said. So the name follows the data rather than the seniority of the widget.

It also left the pie untouched **deliberately**, to avoid re-translating three bundles' worth of strings that were never stale. That is scope discipline I did not specify and would not have thought to.

Confirmed the thing I did ask about: **widget ids are unchanged**, so no translation key, persisted widget state or dataset binding moves.

## The follow-up I want to single out

#8765 does something rare: **it argues against the comfortable reading of its own PR.**

> Before: a source edit left all four bundles stale together. Wrong everywhere, but uniformly, and an English-speaking reviewer looking at the running app could see it.
> After: […] `en` is right and zh-CN / ja-JP / es-ES are wrong. The drift becomes locale-specific and invisible to every reviewer who reads the product in English — which is every reviewer this repo has.
> The gate does not create the drift; it removes the one accidental symptom that used to make it visible.

That is correct, and it is the opposite of how a dev is tempted to describe a gate it just added. Pinning `en` is still right — but it converts a loud-and-uniform failure into a quiet-and-partial one, and saying so is what makes the follow-up card honest rather than decorative. Both #8765 and #8764 verified as actually filed, unassigned, `finding` + `domain:metadata`, with the fence's *"file it separately and link back"* followed to the letter.

#8765 carries a genuine product decision (what a translated locale should do when its source moves: serve stale / fall back to source / fail the build). I am surfacing it to the maintainer rather than grading it here — grading a `finding` is triage's action, not this seat's.

## Housekeeping

- **Docs-drift advisory (2 pages): no action.** The check keys on package touched; this PR changes leaf translation values, two declared title strings and a test. No documented surface moves.
- Same honest disclosure pattern as #8751: `platform-objects` excludes `**/*.test.ts` from its tsconfig, so the new test's types are verified by the `check:type-check-debt` re-measure (which lifts the exclusion) rather than by `pnpm typecheck` — `TEST_DEBT` of 3 unmoved. Stating where the green reading does *not* reach is worth more than the green reading.
- Gates were still running at review time; I'll take job conclusions before marking ready, then auto-merge in that order.
